hero.title: Working of the Constituent Assembly
hero.description: Understand the historic sessions, election of office bearers, Nehru's Objectives Resolution, key committees, administrative staff, and the final adoption of the Indian Constitution.

timeline.title: Chronology of the Constituent Assembly (1946 - 1950)
timeline.description: Trace the historic milestones from the first meeting to the final adoption and signature of the Constitution.

cards.details: Constituent Assembly met for the first time. Boycotted by the Muslim League (demanding a separate state of Pakistan). Only 211 members attended. Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha was elected temporary President.
Dr. Rajendra Prasad was elected as the permanent President of the Assembly. H.C. Mookerjee and V.T. Krishnamachari were elected as the two Vice-Presidents.
Jawaharlal Nehru moved the historic **'Objectives Resolution'**, laying down the guiding philosophy and structural principles for the Constitution.
The Assembly unanimously adopted the Objectives Resolution. It subsequently shaped the Preamble and the entire philosophy of the Constitution.
The Assembly adopted the National Flag of India (designed by Pingali Venkayya) with the Ashoka Chakra.
The Assembly ratified India's membership in the Commonwealth of Nations, preserving sovereign status.
The Constitution was declared passed after three readings. Members signed it, and provisions regarding citizenship, elections, and provisional parliament came into force immediately.
The Assembly held its final session. It adopted the National Anthem, the National Song, and elected Dr. Rajendra Prasad as the first President of India.

mnemonics.title: Mnemonics & Memory Hacks
mnemonics.description: Use these visual memory hooks to retain critical facts about the Constituent Assembly for the UPSC Civil Services Examination.

items.title: Mnemonic 1: Office Bearers
items.decryption: Remember the top three leaders of the Assembly: **P**rasad (President) and the two Vice-Presidents, **M**ookherjee and **K**rishnamachari.

items.title: Mnemonic 2: Staff Roles
items.decryption: Remember the key administrative and drafting figures: Sir B.N. **R**au (Constitutional Advisor), H.V.R. **I**engar (Secretary), and S.N. **M**ukerjee (Chief Draftsman).

items.title: Mnemonic 3: Flag and Anthem Years
items.decryption: The National Flag was adopted in **1947** (before Independence on July 22), whereas the National Anthem and Song were adopted in **1950** (just before Republic Day on Jan 24).

flashcards.title: Active Recall Flashcards
flashcards.description: Use these active recall questions to reinforce fact-dense syllabus details on the working of the assembly.

items.question: Who was the temporary President of the Constituent Assembly, and what practice was followed for this choice?
items.answer: Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha was elected temporary President, following the French practice of electing the oldest member.

items.question: Who were elected as the two Vice-Presidents of the Constituent Assembly?
When was the Objectives Resolution adopted by the Constituent Assembly?
items.answer: It was adopted unanimously on January 22, 1947 (after being introduced on December 13, 1946).

items.question: Who was the Constitutional Advisor to the Constituent Assembly?
items.answer: Sir B.N. Rau was appointed as the Legal Advisor.

items.question: Who was the calligrapher of the original English version of the Indian Constitution?
items.answer: Prem Behari Narain Raizada calligraphed the original text in a flowing italic style.

traps.title: UPSC Prelims Traps to Avoid
items: Trap 1: Do not confuse the dates: the Objectives Resolution was *introduced* on Dec 13, 1946, but *adopted* on Jan 22, 1947. Questions often swap these dates.
Trap 2: The Constituent Assembly did not have just one Vice-President. It had **two** Vice-Presidents: H.C. Mookerjee and V.T. Krishnamachari.
Trap 3: The National Flag was adopted *before* independence (July 22, 1947), but the National Anthem and National Song were adopted *after* independence, just before Republic Day (January 24, 1950).
Trap 4: Sir B.N. Rau was the Legal/Constitutional Advisor, not a member of the Drafting Committee. Do not confuse his role with B.R. Ambedkar (who was Chairman of the Drafting Committee).

deepDive.title: Syllabus Core Study Notes (Deep-Dive)
deepDive.description: Master the structure, timeline, and administrative details of the Constituent Assembly.

sections.title: 1. First Meetings, Office Bearers & Objectives Resolution
sections.content:
The Constituent Assembly held its inaugural session on December 9, 1946, in the Constitution Hall (now Central Hall of Parliament). This first meeting was boycotted by the Muslim League, which insisted on a separate sovereign state of Pakistan; consequently, only 211 members attended. Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha, the oldest member of the Assembly, was elected as the temporary President, adhering to the established French precedent.

Office Bearers Structure

On December 11, 1946, the Assembly elected its permanent leadership and advisory panel:

  • President: Dr. Rajendra Prasad
  • Vice-Presidents: H.C. Mookerjee & V.T. Krishnamachari (dual vice-presidents to represent provincial and princely state interests)
  • Constitutional Advisor: Sir B.N. Rau (prepared the initial draft based on extensive global research)
  • Secretary to Assembly: H.V.R. Iengar
  • Chief Draftsman: S.N. Mukerjee (renowned for putting complex legislative proposals into precise legal language)
Objectives Resolution (Dec 13, 1946)

Jawaharlal Nehru moved the historic Objectives Resolution in the Assembly. It declared India as an independent sovereign republic and laid down the principles of justice, equality, freedom, and protection for minorities. It was unanimously adopted on January 22, 1947, and its modified version forms the **Preamble** of the Indian Constitution.

Structure of the Constituent Assembly's Leadership

sections.title: 2. Major Committees, Other Functions & Final Adoption
sections.content:
The Constituent Assembly appointed several committees to deal with different tasks of constitution-making. Among these, eight were Major Committees and the rest were Minor Committees. The Assembly also performed crucial state functions beyond constitution drafting.

The 8 Major Committees (UPSC High-Yield)
  • Drafting Committee: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar (7 members, scrutinized the draft)
  • Union Powers Committee: Jawaharlal Nehru
  • Union Constitution Committee: Jawaharlal Nehru
  • Provincial Constitution Committee: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel
  • Advisory Committee on FRs, Minorities & Tribal Areas: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel
  • Rules of Procedure Committee: Dr. Rajendra Prasad
  • States Committee (Negotiating with States): Jawaharlal Nehru
  • Steering Committee: Dr. Rajendra Prasad
Other Functions & Key Statistics

In addition to drafting the Constitution, the Assembly:

  • Ratified India's Commonwealth membership in May 1949.
  • Adopted the National Flag on July 22, 1947.
  • Adopted the National Anthem and National Song on January 24, 1950.
  • Elected Dr. Rajendra Prasad as the first President of India on January 24, 1950.
  • Took 2 years, 11 months, and 18 days, held 11 sessions, and cost Rs. 64 lakh.
Artistic & Calligraphic Details

The original Constitution was a masterpiece of calligraphy and design. **Prem Behari Narain Raizada** calligraphed the original English version in flowing italic handwriting. **Vasant Krishan Vaidya** calligraphed the Hindi translation. The pages were decorated and illuminated by artists from Shantiniketan, led by **Nandlal Bose** and **Beohar Rammanohar Sinha** (who decorated the Preamble page). The assembly adopted the **Elephant** as its seal.
